newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-GANGULY HAMMERS 85-BALL CENTURY. [CORRECTED 20:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-GANGULY HAMMERS 85-BALL CENTURY. [CORRECTED 20:40 GMT]

text.p: A swashbuckling century by Saurav Ganguly led India to a seven-wicket win over Griqualand West on Thursday.
Ganguly made 101 from just 85 balls with five sixes and eight fours as the touring team coasted to their target of 206 with 15.2 overs (corrects from 15 balls) to spare.
Ganguly put on 94 for the first wicket with Sachin Tendulkar, before refusing a call for a single which saw his captain run out for a fluent 51 from 49 balls.
The Calcutta left-hander went on to dominate a 93-run stand for the second wicket with Rahul Dravid before holing out to off-spinner Martyn Gidley attempting yet another big hit.
Gidley also picked up the prize wicket of Mohammad Azharuddin, caught at point for one, but Dravid saw his side to victory with a composed unbeaten 25.

Griqualand West's 205 for seven was built around half centuries by Pieter Barnard and Willie Dry. The pair put on 123 for the third wicket before Barnard hit a looping catch to mid-on after scoring 54 from 104 balls.
His departure signalled a collapse that saw five wickets fall for 23 runs. Dry top-scored with a well crafted 72 from 85 balls with five fours and two sixes.
India now move on to Bloemfontein where they will play a three-ay match against Free State beginning on Saturday.
